issues.problem: -aḥ cannot be genitive plural (that is vājinām). It is nom./acc. pl. or gen./abl. sg.; the draft's 'of the prize-winners' rests on an impossible label. Nom. pl. 'we prize-winners' (with śakema) is one real option, gen. sg. 'of the prize-winner' another; needs a human choice.
issues.fix: m. nom./acc. pl. or gen./abl. sg.

patch.value: m. nom. pl. or gen. sg. (not gen. pl.)

issues.problem: yakṣan is not a present participle (that would be yajan); it is an s-aorist/injunctive or infinitive-type form of pra-√yaj.
issues.fix: form of pra-√yaj (not a pres. part.)

issues.problem: Not a typo (the flag says 'not an error'); the inserted t is regular Vedic sandhi.
English and notes read raśmi as 'rein'; रश्मि in Hindi means ray.

issues.problem: Glossary: Praśāstṛ priest (the draft's own note concedes this).
Praśāstṛ priest (प्रशास्ता) and kratu = resolve (संकल्प) per glossary.
'जो ... है' adds a relative clause; the text has only neṣṭuḥ (genitive).

Hindi turns kuvit into a question and adds a second verb 'गईं'; English reads 'Indeed, the sisters who went to this one, from the three to the better'. The two layers disagree and the Hindi adds a verb.
